title: Multimodal Assessment of Cerebrovascular Reserve in Neurovascular Diseases
summary:
In several diseases affecting the blood vessels supplying the brain, the ability to increase cerebral blood flow when needed may be impaired. This capacity is known as cerebrovascular reserve and may provide important information about stroke risk and disease progression.

The aim of this study is to evaluate a new non-invasive MRI technique that measures cerebrovascular reserve without the need for medication or contrast agents. During the MRI examination, participants repeatedly hold their breath for a few seconds. In addition, an ultrasound examination of the cerebral arteries is performed. Results will be compared between patients with neurovascular diseases and healthy volunteers and will also be assessed over time.

The long-term goal is to determine whether this method can improve diagnostic assessment and support future treatment decisions.
conditions: stenoses of brain arteries, Moyamoya, AVM

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients:
- Age ≥18 years
- Written informed consent
- Presence of one of the following neurovascular diseases:
≥50% stenosis of the internal carotid artery or middle cerebral artery,
Moyamoya disease or comparable angiopathy,
arteriovenous malformation (AVM)

Healthy volunteers:
- Age ≥18 years
- Written informed consent
- No known neurovascular disease
Exclusion criteria:
The following exclusion criteria apply to both patients and healthy volunteers:
- Inability to provide informed consent
- Refusal or withdrawal of informed consent
- Severe pulmonary disease
- Brain tumors, chronic inflammatory brain diseases, or other neurological disorders that may substantially interfere with assessment of cerebrovascular reserve
- Contraindications to MRI, including:
Cardiac pacemakers or other non-MRI-compatible implants
Ferromagnetic foreign bodies
Pregnancy, breastfeeding, or pregnancy that cannot be excluded
Severe claustrophobia
